subject: Pipeline scaling & throttle alignment for Kappa AI integration
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.inference>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam@kappa.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@kappa.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 12 Apr 2025 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: pipeline scaling & initial rate/connection asks

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — good conversation. Quick recap so we have an actionable set of asks and constraints on our side for the Redwood sizing / rate proposal. Please confirm if I've captured everything correctly.

Summary of Kappa requirements (from discovery)
- Expected sustained read/write traffic: ~120 requests/sec (rps) during business hours
- Burst profile: spikes up to ~500 rps for up to 5 minutes, occasionally (startups-style flash events)
- Latency SLO target: p95 generation latency <= 250 ms for single-turn requests; streaming responses allowed for long polls
- Concurrency/parallelism: up to ~40 in-flight parallel generation requests per customer instance (these are independent HTTP calls; some long-poll streaming)
- Connection model: you plan to use long-lived HTTP/2 + multiplexing from your edge, with 8–12 persistent connections per region for redundancy
- Streaming requirements: server-side chunked responses with early tokens matter (so partials should arrive within 100–150ms of generation start)

Questions for Redwood (what we'd like you to propose)
1) Rate limits & quota model: how do you recommend mapping the above to per-route rate limits vs connection-based quotas? We need a recommended default throttle to include in our integration guide.
2) Failure & fallback behavior: if we exceed reserved capacity, what fallback model do you propose (throttling vs auto-fallback to smaller model vs queued retries)?
3) Sizing recommendation: hosted vs dedicated sizing given the burst pattern — what committed rps and burst windows would you recommend to hit p95 250ms?
4) Cost impact: top-level estimate (monthly) for sustained 120 rps + periodic bursts (include cost delta if we opt for Dedicated)

Attachments: I mentioned we'd share a short SLO matrix and an initial ratecard — attaching the SLO matrix for context (slo-matrix.xlsx).

Next steps
- Redwood: propose a rate/connection model and a high-level sizing + offer for a 1-week trial profile (we're hoping to validate with traffic from our staging cluster first)
- Kappa: confirm whether the burst profile is representative and whether you can provide short traces for the demo run

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30-min follow-up next week if that helps.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.inference
From: Liam O'Neill <liam@kappa.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@kappa.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 12 Apr 2025 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pipeline scaling & initial rate/connection asks

Thanks Rohan — this is helpful and aligns with our notes. A couple quick clarifications before the Redwood sizing: 

1) When you say "40 in-flight parallel generation requests per customer instance", is that the maximum concurrency per model endpoint or total across endpoints? For Kappa we'll likely open multiple endpoints (embedding, chat, rerank) from the same service pool.
2) How do you treat HTTP/2 multiplexed streams for quota accounting? Is each stream billed/limited as a separate request or do you prefer connection-based quotas?

Also can you share the rate card and a sample SLA wording for the trial? We'll want to fold that into our procurement note.

Happy to do the follow-up call — Monday or Tuesday afternoon PT works for Sanjay and me.

— Liam
Product Lead, Kappa AI
liam@kappa.ai
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam@kappa.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@kappa.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Apr 2025 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pipeline scaling & initial rate/connection asks

Marissa / Monica — looping you in with a recommended negotiation posture and the specifics Liam asked for; copying the external thread so they have visibility. Draft proposal below that we can present to Kappa.

High-level negotiation approach
- Offer a 2-stage quota plan: STAGING (trial) + PRODUCTION commit. Staging gives Kappa the ability to validate behavior without a long-term commit.

Recommended quota mapping (initial proposal)
- Staging trial: 100 rps sustained, burst up to 400 rps for 10 minutes/day (free trial with monitoring)
- Production guaranteed: 300 rps sustained per account, soft-burst to 800 rps for up to 5 minutes (subject to capacity); hard enforced throttle at 1,200 rps if extreme
- Concurrency guidance: recommend customers open ~6 HTTP/2 connections with multiplexing; treat each request stream as a request for quota accounting (we charge/limit per request). Provide sample connection pool settings in the integration guide (maxConcurrentStreams ~100, idle timeout 60s).

SLO & fallback
- SLO: p95 <= 250 ms for single-turn within the production plan; streaming latency best-effort but we will instrument first-byte latency for streaming tokens and alert at 150ms median deviance.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to a smaller model family for non-critical endpoints, or queueing with exponential backoff for critical endpoints. We'll include an automatic model-fallback policy in the trial config.

Cost ballpark (monthly)
- Hosted (no commit): approx $Xk/month for sustained 120 rps + burst usage; will provide a concrete number in the ratecard doc
- Dedicated (committed): higher baseline infra fee but discounts on token/unit pricing; recommend Dedicated if Kappa wants guaranteed latency during bursts regularly.

Attachments: attaching the redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf and the SLO matrix for the call material.

Next steps (internal)
- Marissa: please prepare a short one-pager that maps staging trial -> production commit including the test run checklist and instrumentation hooks.
- Monica: prep a short demo runbook and ensure we can enable 300 rps in the staging cluster on Monday for the trial.
- Rohan: propose 2x time slots for Monday/Tuesday for the follow-up.

— Rohan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@kappa.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.inference>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam@kappa.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 13 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pipeline scaling & initial rate/connection asks

Thanks — this looks reasonable and gives us the flexibility we need. A few quick notes from Kappa: 

- We're comfortable validating in the staging trial with 100 rps and will plan to push a short spike test at 400 rps the first day. For production we'd prefer guaranteed 300 rps with soft-burst to 800 rps as proposed.
- For billing/procurement: can Redwood provide a short addendum that codifies the production rate caps and the credit terms if SLOs are missed during the committed window? Procurement will need that to move the PO forward.
- We'll share a short traffic dump for the demo (traces + token distribution) before Monday so you can test the streaming token behavior.

Availability: Monday 2025-04-14 11:00–12:00 PT or Tuesday 2025-04-15 14:00–15:00 PT — either works for us. Please confirm a slot and a Dial/Zoom link.
